ABOUT US¶

  • We are a team of aspiring data analysts and machine learning practitioners passionate about uncovering insights through data. This project is part of our academic journey to apply statistical and machine learning techniques to real-world datasets and solve meaningful business problems.

  • In this project, we explored various statistical tests and unsupervised learning methods to analyze customer behavior, segment populations, and identify key patterns in health insurance and wholesale purchasing data. Our goal is to bridge the gap between raw data and informed decision-making using tools like Python, pandas, seaborn, scikit-learn, and more.

In [123]:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import warnings
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.cluster import DBSCAN
import scipy.cluster.hierarchy as sch
from sklearn.cluster import AgglomerativeClustering
from sklearn.metrics import silhouette_score
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.cluster import SpectralClustering
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

Histogram (Distribution of individual features)¶

In [10]:
data.hist(bins=20, figsize=(12, 8), color='limegreen') 
plt.suptitle("Histograms of All Features", fontsize=16)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
  • This code generates histograms for all numerical features in the dataset, allowing us to visually assess the distribution of each variable.

Boxplot (Detecting outliers)¶

In [12]:
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.boxplot(data=data.drop(columns=["Channel", "Region"]))
plt.title("Boxplot of Numerical Features")
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.show()
  • This boxplot visualizes the distribution, spread, and outliers for each numerical feature (excluding Channel and Region) in the dataset.

Pairplot¶

In [14]:
sns.pairplot(
    data[['Fresh', 'Milk', 'Grocery', 'Frozen', 'Detergents_Paper', 'Delicassen', 'Region']],
    hue='Region',
    palette='Set2'
)
Out[14]:
<seaborn.axisgrid.PairGrid at 0x1868a12c830>
  • This pairplot visualizes pairwise relationships between the six main spending categories (Fresh, Milk, Grocery, Frozen, Detergents_Paper, Delicassen), with points color-coded by Region.

Correlation Heatmap¶

In [16]:
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.heatmap(data.corr(), annot=True, cmap='YlGnBu', fmt=".2f")
plt.title("Correlation Heatmap")
plt.show()
  • The correlation heatmap reveals the linear relationships between different numerical features in the Wholesale Customers dataset.

Countplot for Categorical Variables¶

In [18]:
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4))
sns.countplot(x='Channel', data=data, ax=axes[0],palette='Blues')
axes[0].set_title('Channel Count')
sns.countplot(x='Region', data=data, ax=axes[1],palette='Oranges')
axes[1].set_title('Region Count')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
  • This visualization provides a quick overview of how customers are distributed across different Channels and Regions in the dataset.

PCA¶

  • PCA (Principal Component Analysis) is a dimensionality reduction technique used in data analysis and machine learning to simplify large datasets while preserving as much information (variance) as possible.
In [22]:

pca.fit(scaled_data)

DBSCAN¶

  • DBSCAN stands for Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise. It is an unsupervised clustering algorithm used to group data points that are closely packed together, while marking points in low-density areas as outliers (noise).
In [29]:
dbscan=DBSCAN(eps=0.5,min_samples=5)
labels=dbscan.fit_predict(x_pca1)

colors = [plt.cm.Spectral(each) for each in np.linspace(0, 1, len(set(labels)))]

for k, col in zip(set(labels), colors):
    if k == -1:
        col = [0, 0, 0, 1]  

    class_member_mask = (labels == k)
    xy = x_pca1[class_member_mask]

    xy = np.atleast_2d(xy)  
    plt.plot(xy[:, 0], xy[:, 1], 'o',
             markerfacecolor=tuple(col),
             markeredgecolor='k',
             markersize=10)

plt.title("DBSCAN Clustering on Customer Data")
plt.xlabel("PCA - 1")
plt.ylabel("PCA - 2")
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()

Agglomerative Clustering¶

  • Agglomerative Clustering is a type of Hierarchical Clustering that builds clusters from the bottom up. It starts by treating each data point as its own cluster and then merges the closest clusters step by step until all points belong to a single cluster or a stopping condition is met.
In [35]:
dendrogram=sch.dendrogram(sch.linkage(data,method='ward'))
plt.title('dendrogram')
plt.xlabel('data points')
plt.ylabel('euclidean distance')
plt.show()
In [36]:
ahc=AgglomerativeClustering(n_clusters=3,metric='euclidean',linkage='ward')
y_ahc=ahc.fit_predict(data)

KMEANS¶

In [41]:
wcss = []
k_range = range(1, 11)
In [42]:
for k in k_range:
    kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=k, random_state=42)
    kmeans.fit(x_pca)
    wcss.append(kmeans.inertia_)

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
plt.plot(k_range, wcss, marker='o')
plt.xlabel('Number of Clusters (k)')
plt.ylabel('Inertia')
plt.title('Elbow Method to Find Optimal k')
plt.show()

kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=optimal_k, random_state=42)

SpectralClustering¶

  • Spectral Clustering is an unsupervised machine learning algorithm used to group data points into clusters based on the structure of the data. It is particularly effective for identifying non-convex, complex-shaped clusters that traditional methods like KMeans may not detect well.
